crossTeamComparison.summary: Three distinct performance profiles. VitalHire leads on organizational grounding and writing quality. Team X leads on scope and specificity (especially exclusions and data inputs). Team Y has one strong section (Decision Authority) surrounded by significant gaps, with the Purpose section being a near-total miss.

system_purpose.note: Massive spread. VitalHire opens with Lakeside numbers. Team X uses 'claims' language correctly. Team Y wrote generic software copy with zero organizational specificity.

decision_authority.note: Closest category. All three understand the recommendation-not-decision distinction. Team X and Team Y mention audit trails. VitalHire is clear but missing process mechanics.

users_affected.note: VitalHire's mapping is cleanest -- correct HM classification, departments as downstream affected. Team X and Team Y both have the HM-in-both-columns problem.

data_inputs.note: Team X has the most specificity -- ATS integration, recruiter feedback loop, configuration settings. VitalHire and Team Y both go thin on configuration parameters.

exclusions.note: Strongest category across all teams. Team X has nine grounded exclusions. VitalHire has the EEOC compliance gap insight. Team Y covers the basics well.

exec_comm.note: Team X and VitalHire maintain professional register throughout. Team Y is inconsistent -- Decision Authority reads executive-level while Purpose reads undergraduate.

emergingPatterns: Exclusions is the strongest category across all three teams. Students understand 'what does this system NOT do' better than 'what problem does it solve.' Interesting -- negative scope is clearer to them than positive scope.

Users vs. Affected Parties is the most commonly confused area. Two of three teams put hiring managers in the wrong column or in both columns. The user/affected distinction needs reinforcement before WK11.

AI tool usage varies: Team X and Team Y disclosed ChatGPT for language polish on specific sections. VitalHire used it only for organization. Team Y's no-additional-sources combined with ChatGPT for language raises the question of whether the content or just the polish came from AI.

Team Y's performance gap is structural, not cosmetic. The Purpose section failure cascades -- without organizational grounding, the rest of the document floats. This team needs intervention before WK11 or the risk matrix will be equally unmoored.

Individual contribution distribution: VitalHire's Barber is carrying (Lead Author + Visual + compiled final doc). Team Y's Allen wrote the only strong section plus the visual. Both flagged as CARRYING.
